stories.headline: Who is Qiulae Wong? New Zealand's potential kingmaker after cliffhanger election
stories.deck: Qiulae Wong, a 38-year-old politician who entered politics less than a year ago, could emerge as a kingmaker in New Zealand after the general election delivered no clear winner. Her centrist Opportunity Party is projected to win seven seats, potentially giving it a decisive role in government formation. Wong's party is pushing sweeping tax reforms, including a universal basic income funded by a…
stories.bodyText:
Qiulae Wong has been in politics for less than a year, but the 38-year-old could emerge as a key power broker in New Zealand's parliament after the initial counting in Saturday's general election ended without a clear winner.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right coalition could secure a majority of just two seats, according to preliminary results released by the Electoral Commission. However, that narrow lead could disappear once special votes, which typically favour the left, are included in the official count due on November 27.
If that happens, either the centre-right or centre-left bloc could need the support of Wong's centrist Opportunity Party, which is on course to enter parliament for the first time. Luxon's National Party and the Labour Party, led by Chris Hipkins, are expected to explore coalition options in the coming days and weeks.
Wong, a former sustainable-business consultant, took charge of the decade-old Opportunity Party in November 2025 after responding to an advertisement seeking a new leader.
She quickly oversaw a rebranding exercise and a dramatic rise in the party's popularity. With its vote share currently at 5.96%, Opportunity is projected to win seven seats in the 131-member parliament, Electoral Commission data showed.
Addressing supporters in Auckland on Saturday night, Wong described the result as the culmination of years of political groundwork.
"It might seem like we've just arrived, that this is an overnight success, but to many in this room, this result has been a long time coming," Wong told cheering supporters in Auckland on Saturday night.
Opportunity Party's sweeping tax proposals
The Opportunity Party's flagship agenda revolves around a major overhaul of New Zealand's tax system. Its key proposal is an annual 
universal basic income
 of NZ$19,400 ($10,800) for most New Zealand residents, funded through a 1.75% annual land tax.
The party also wants to simplify the country's income tax structure, shifting a greater share of the tax burden from earnings to wealth and property.
“There's also been a shift globally around seeing the need to tax work less and tax wealth more or tax assets more. And so that's what this tax reset package is designed to do: take some of the burden off income tax and place that onto property,” Wong told Reuters in an interview in August.
If implemented, the universal basic income proposal would be a first for a developed economy. While land taxes are used in dozens of countries, they generally exempt primary residences, unlike the Opportunity Party's proposal.
However, the party could face resistance from both major political blocs. National and Labour have ruled out adopting its tax proposals, while Luxon has repeatedly said during the election campaign that he would not enter into a coalition with Opportunity.
Wong keeps coalition options open
Despite the political differences, Wong has indicated that she is open to negotiations with whichever party wins the largest number of seats in parliament. She has maintained that the Opportunity Party could find common ground with either National or Labour.
Outlining the possible arrangements, Wong told public broadcaster TVNZ on Saturday:
"There are different forms of us working with other parties, whether that's coalition, confidence and supply, being on the crossbenches, and all of those options are on the table for us right now," she told public broadcaster TVNZ on Saturday.
She added that the final decision would depend on the election outcome.
"We have to we have to look at how the votes land."

stories.headline: Rereading the menu after ordering isn't indecisiveness, psychology says
stories.deck: When confronted with an abundance of menu options, many diners experience uncertainty in their choices. Research indicates that the way individuals make decisions can greatly affect their levels of regret and satisfaction. Maximisers meticulously analyze their options, while satisficers opt for choices that are ‘good enough’. By establishing preferences in advance and restricting options, diners…
stories.bodyText:
You are sitting at a restaurant with friends. You have looked through the menu, settled on a dish and are almost ready to place your order. But when the waiter approaches, you glance at the menu again. You read the options once more, compare a couple of dishes and briefly wonder whether you should order something else.
You may eventually choose the same dish you had decided on minutes earlier. Yet, for some reason, you needed to check the menu again.
This familiar habit may have something to do with decision uncertainty. It does not necessarily mean that you do not know what you want. Sometimes, the difficulty lies in feeling confident that the choice you have made is the right one.
The feeling that there might be a better option
Photo: Canva
A restaurant menu presents several possibilities at once. Even after finding something appealing, you may notice another dish that sounds equally good, costs less or seems more interesting. That can make you question your original choice.
Research on choice overload helps explain why this happens. A 
2015 meta-analysis
 published in the Journal of Consumer Psychology examined 99 observations involving 7,202 participants.
The researchers found that having more options can make decisions harder under certain conditions. 
The effect was influenced by factors such as how complicated the choices were, how difficult the decision felt and how certain people were about their preferences.
In other words, a long menu may be particularly challenging when you are not completely sure what you feel like eating. Going through it again can become an attempt to reduce that uncertainty.
When choosing the best option becomes more important than choosing something good
Another possible explanation comes from research on two decision-making styles: maximising and satisficing. Maximisers tend to search for the best possible option. They compare alternatives and may continue looking even after finding something they like. Satisficers, on the other hand, are more likely to choose an option that meets their requirements and move on.
Psychologists explored this difference in a 
2002 paper
. Across several studies, the researchers found that people with stronger maximising tendencies reported more regret and were less satisfied with consumer decisions than those who were less focused on finding the absolute best option.
Applied to a restaurant setting, this could mean that someone has already selected a dish they would enjoy but continues scanning the menu because they want to make sure another option would not have been better. The issue is not necessarily the food. It is the possibility of missing out on a better choice.
Why you may question your decision even after making it
Photo: Canva
Decision-making does not always end when a person selects an option. People can continue thinking about alternatives they did not choose. 
A study in 2021
 examined how people evaluated their decisions when faced with too many options. It found that maximisers reported more negative post-decision evaluations than satisficers during choice overload.
This helps explain why someone might revisit a menu even after mentally placing an order. They may be checking whether their choice still feels like the best one, rather than looking for something entirely different.
However, repeatedly reading a menu does not automatically mean someone has a maximising personality. Hunger, unfamiliar dishes, dietary preferences, prices, the people they are dining with and simply enjoying browsing can all influence the behaviour.
How to stop turning a simple meal into a difficult decision
If you recognise this habit in yourself, a few small changes may help:
- Decide what matters before opening the menu: Think about your budget, appetite and the kind of food you want.
- Shortlist two or three dishes: You do not need to compare every item on the page.
- Look for what you will enjoy, not what you might be missing: Another dish sounding good does not make your first choice a bad one.
- Give yourself permission to settle: If a dish meets your expectations, you can choose it without proving that it is the best item on the menu.
There is no established psychological rule that rereading a menu after deciding is a sign of decision uncertainty. The studies above examine broader patterns of choice, comparison and regret rather than this specific restaurant habit.
Still, the next time you find yourself reading the same menu for the third time, it may be worth asking whether you are genuinely reconsidering your order or simply looking for reassurance that you have chosen well.

stories.headline: FSSAI seizes 3,280 tonne food items, cancels 52 licences in nationwide inspection drive
stories.deck: The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets
stories.bodyText:
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has seized 3,280 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹82 crore during its nationwide inspection drive, which began on September 1 to check adulteration during the festive season.
Acting against food safety violations, the FSSAI cancelled 52 licences, suspended 1,133 licences, and sealed 314 establishments.
In a social media post on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the FSSAI said that it has stepped up vigilance in view of festivals.
The regulator said it inspected 56,431 food establishments during its nationwide enforcement drive between September 1 and November 5, and seized non-compliant food products, including paneer, ghee, milk and sweets.
A total of 3,279.57 tonnes of 'banned and non-compliant' food products worth ₹81.80 crore were seized, it said.
Additionally, the regulator issued 10,047 improvement notices to food business operators.
This calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators and e-commerce companies to ensure safe food for consumers.

stories.headline: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
stories.deck: The accused fired several rounds at the victim and his son; the victim succumbed to injuries and the son escaped unhurt
stories.bodyText:
A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.
According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.
An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.
“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.
A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Published - November 08, 2026 04:32 am IST

briefs.headline: PM Modi extends Diwali greetings, to celebrate with Army jawans
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Prime Minister Narendra Modi
 on Sunday extended Diwali greetings to people across the country, wishing them happiness, peace and prosperity on the occasion of the festival of lights.
In a post on X, PM Modi wrote, “Diwali wishes to everyone! Boundless Diwali wishes to my family members across the country.”
On Saturday, the Prime Minister had also shared a video message extending his wishes to the people and describing Diwali as a symbol of the country's resolve against darkness.
“Hello! The holy festival of Diwali, the whole country is lit up with lights. This festival of light is an introduction to our resolve against darkness. Wishing you all a very Happy Diwali. May this festival of yours, your future time be filled with happiness, peace and prosperity,” he said.
PM Modi also reiterated his tradition of celebrating Diwali with jawans, saying he would continue the practice this year as well.
“Like you, I celebrate Diwali with great enthusiasm, and as you know, it has become a tradition for me to spend this day among our jawans, a practice I will continue this year as well. Once again, my best wishes to you all for Diwali!” he said.
Earlier, the Prime Minister met Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and exchanged Diwali greetings. 
Sharing details of the meeting on X, PM Modi wrote, “Met Vice President Thiru CP Radhakrishnan Ji and exchanged Diwali greetings.”
Meanwhile, BJP national president Nitin Nabin also extended Diwali greetings to the nation on Saturday and urged people to embrace Modi's 'Vocal for Local' vision by purchasing products made by local shopkeepers and artisans.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
In a festive video message shared on X, Nabin said collective consumer choices during the festival would help lay the foundation for an Atmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.
Recalling the significance of Diwali, he referred to Lord Ram's return to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and linked the occasion to the modern renaissance of the Ram Temple.
The five-day Diwali celebrations began with Dhanteras on November 6, followed by Choti Diwali on November 7. The main festival and Lakshmi Puja are being observed on Sunday, followed by Govardhan Puja on November 9 and Bhai Dooj on November 10.

briefs.headline: Wife stabs ex-Army man to death: How a 'cooked veggie' for dinner led to murder
briefs.deck: A woman allegedly stabbed her husband during a heated argument over dinner in Ahmedabad. The couple had reportedly been arguing over domestic matters for nearly a year. After the incident, the woman informed her brother-in-law about the stabbing and stated her husband had become unconscious. Despite being rushed to the hospital, the husband unfortunately succumbed to his injuries.
briefs.bodyText:
AHMEDABAD: A dinner-time argument over a vegetable cooked at home allegedly ended in murder in Ahmedabad's Naroda, where a 34-year-old woman is accused of stabbing her husband, a retired Army serviceman, in the chest with a kitchen knife.
Dilip Kharadi, 39, who worked as a contractual driver with Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC), was rushed to Shalby Hospital but succumbed to his injuries.
Police arrested his wife, Nirmala Kharadi, and registered a murder case against her. The couple's two children are now left without their father, while their mother remains in police custody.
Argument over dinner escalated into fatal confrontation
The incident took place around midnight on Thursday at the couple's residence in Naroda Smart City-2. According to Naroda police inspector B M Katariya, the couple had reportedly been arguing frequently over domestic and financial matters for nearly a year.
The latest confrontation allegedly began when Dilip questioned his wife about the particular vegetable she had prepared for dinner. The disagreement escalated into a heated exchange, with both allegedly abusing each other.
Police said Nirmala subsequently picked up a kitchen knife and stabbed Dilip on the left side of his chest.
Katariya said investigators would question the accused to establish the sequence of events and what exactly led to the fatal confrontation.
Woman allegedly informed brother-in-law about stabbing
The incident came to light after Nirmala allegedly called her brother-in-law, Mukesh, around midnight and told him that she had stabbed Dilip in the chest during an argument.
She allegedly informed him that her husband had become unconscious and that she was taking him to Shalby Hospital for treatment.
On Friday afternoon, Mukesh informed his father, Somaji Kharadi, that Dilip had been injured in a quarrel and was admitted to hospital. Somaji, 73, accompanied by other family members, rushed there.
However, doctors informed the family that Dilip had succumbed to his injuries.
Father noticed stab wound and other injuries
According to the complaint filed by Somaji, a retired unarmed assistant sub-inspector with Rajkot city police, he noticed a stab wound on the left side of his son's chest.
He also found injuries on Dilip's right cheek, right upper arm and near the thumbs of both hands.
The family had initially withheld the news of Dilip's death from Somaji, fearing that the news would come as a shock to him.
Dilip had retired from the Army in 2022 and was subsequently working as a contractual driver with GMDC.
Police teams traced accused within hours
Following the incident, Naroda police formed multiple teams to trace the accused. Investigators analysed CCTV footage from the area and gathered local intelligence as part of the search.
Nirmala was arrested within hours of the crime.
Police have registered a murder case against her, along with offences under the Gujarat Police Act. The investigation is underway, and the accused is being questioned about the circumstances leading to the stabbing.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu's comeback bid: What happens if Eisenkot fails to form govt in Israel
briefs.deck: Gadi Eisenkot has been tasked with forming a new government after the recent elections. His coalition currently lacks the required seats for a majority, presenting significant challenges. Possible support from Arab parties or ultra-Orthodox factions could aid his efforts. If unsuccessful within 42 days, Benjamin Netanyahu may receive another chance to form a government. This political situation…
briefs.bodyText:
Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has been given the first opportunity to form the next government after President Isaac Herzog invited him on Saturday. The inconclusive October 27 election failed to give any party a clear parliamentary majority.
However, with his coalition falling short of the numbers needed to govern, Eisenkot faces several challenges.
He has options laid out to form a minority government. He can secure support from Arab parties, reach an understanding with ultra-Orthodox factions or explore a broader unity arrangement.
But if he fails within the 42-day deadline, the incumbent Israeli Prime Minister 
Benjamin Netanyahu
 could get another chance to form a government.
Eisenkot's Yashar party and its potential allies have 48 seats in the 120-member parliament.
While his seats fall short of the 61-seat majority mark required, support from Israel's two Arab parties, which together hold 19 seats, could help his bloc reach 67. The parties could support his government from outside without formally joining the coalition, allowing Eisenkot to attempt a minority government.
How Eisenkot can form a minority government
One possibility is for Eisenkot to bring together his natural allies, including the centre-right Together party, The Democrats and Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home. 
Their combined strength stands at 48 seats.
The two Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, could then provide outside support. Both have endorsed Eisenkot to form the next government and expressed willingness to work with his broader camp to prevent Netanyahu's return to power.
However, this arrangement faces political hurdles. Eisenkot had pledged during his campaign not to include Arab parties in his government. Reversing that position could prove difficult, particularly after the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack hardened attitudes towards Israel's Arab minority.
Lieberman has also repeatedly ruled out forming a minority government with Arab parties. So far, only The Democrats, a centre-left party, have publicly supported their inclusion.
Netanyahu has also focused his campaign on delegitimising any government that relies on Arab support.
There is a precedent for such an arrangement. Ra'am joined former prime minister Naftali Bennett's government in 2021. Bennett, who now heads the Together party, is among Eisenkot's potential partners. However, that government collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.
Can ultra-Orthodox parties give Eisenkot a majority
Another option is to seek support from Israel's two ultra-Orthodox parties, which together hold 13 seats. Their backing could take Eisenkot's bloc to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government.
However, reaching an agreement will not be easy. The main sticking point is military service exemptions traditionally granted to ultra-Orthodox seminary students. The exemptions have drawn criticism from many Israelis who believe the burden of military service is unfairly placed on the wider population.
Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have strongly opposed these exemptions. However, Lieberman signalled some flexibility on Friday, saying he was open to a compromise.
"You cannot have it all", he told supporters.
The two ultra-Orthodox parties have also taken different positions following the election. United Torah Judaism declined to endorse any candidate, while Shas backed Netanyahu.
What happens if Eisenkot fails
Eisenkot has up to 42 days to form a government. If he cannot secure the necessary support, Herzog is likely to invite Netanyahu to make another attempt.
Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc has been reduced from its original 64 seats to 53. Despite this, the prime minister could try to weaken the opposition by persuading lawmakers from rival parties to defect and join his camp.
He has used this strategy before. In the run-up to the 2022 election, Netanyahu managed to destabilise the government he was opposing by drawing support away from its ranks. However, the opposition bloc at the time had a much narrower lead, meaning fewer defections were needed to bring it down.
If Netanyahu gets another opportunity, he would need to find enough support to rebuild a parliamentary majority.
Could a unity government emerge
If Eisenkot cannot form a government with Arab or ultra-Orthodox support, another possibility is a unity arrangement involving his Yashar party, Together, Israel Our Home and Netanyahu's Likud.
Likud emerged as the largest party in the October 27 election with 27 seats. A grouping involving these parties would command 67 seats, giving it a parliamentary majority.
However, this appears unlikely for now. Eisenkot and his partners would have to abandon their central campaign promise of removing Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu, in turn, would likely have to distance himself from his traditional far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies.
Still, prolonged coalition negotiations or renewed fighting with Iran could push the rival camps towards a unity arrangement.
Could Israel face another election
If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form a government, parliament can nominate another candidate. The process has a deadline of around 100 days. If no candidate succeeds, Israel will have to hold another election.
Herzog has already warned against another vote. On Wednesday, he said everything must be done to avoid fresh elections and urged political parties to approach consultations with an open mind.

briefs.headline: Double entries, duplicate IDs: Karnataka CEO admits SIR lapses
briefs.deck: Karnataka has identified issues with duplicate voter IDs affecting electors across different assembly constituencies. Procedures allowed applicants to submit multiple Form 6 applications, resulting in separate EPIC numbers. Additionally, voters changing addresses saw their names listed in both their new and old constituencies. Corrections are underway, as cases have been referred to various…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Duplicate voter ID numbers and same electors appearing on the rolls of two different assembly constituencies have surfaced in Karnataka, following special intensive revision (SIR), with chief electoral officer (CEO) acknowledging procedural lapses in processing applications.
In a clarification issued Saturday, the CEO’s office said the discrepancies came to light through two separate lapses in handling voter applications.
In the first instance, some applicants submitted multiple Form 6 applications through the Citizen Service Portal during SIR. Since each application was processed independently, multiple Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers were inadvertently generated for the same voter.
The roll mix-up
The second issue involved voters moving their residences from one assembly constituency to another.
While their Form 8 applications seeking transfer of address were approved and their names added to new constituency’s rolls, corresponding Form 7 applications seeking deletion from the previous constituency remained pending, leading to their names appearing on the rolls at both the addresses.
The cases have now been referred to district election officers, additional district election officers and electoral registration officers for verification and corrective action in accordance with the law.
However, the clarification from the CEO’s office did not say how many voters were affected, how many duplicate entries were identified for deletion, or when the corrections would be made. It also did not clarify whether these discrepancies had affected the final electoral rolls.
It attributed the delay in carrying out corrective measures to a statutory freeze on electoral roll changes ahead of their final publication.

briefs.headline: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
briefs.deck: In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm
briefs.bodyText:
Prosecutors in Paraguay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) charged recently deposed former President Santiago Peña with two crimes linked to the collapse of a major bank that has jeopardised the savings of hundreds of thousands of account holders and unleashed the nation's biggest political crisis in a decade.
In a press conference on Saturday (November 7), Nancy Salomón, the South American nation's chief prosecutor for corruption and economic crimes, said Mr. Peña would be investigated for the crimes of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.
Mr. Peña's removal marks a major crisis for Paraguay, which returned to democratic rule in 1989. Since then, the nation of six million people has been mostly governed by the conservative Colorado Party, of which Mr. Peña was a member.
Prosecutors said the former President could face up to 20 years in prison if he is found guilty of both crimes and have asked a judge to freeze Mr. Peña's assets and send him to prison while investigations continue.
Later on Saturday (November 7), Paraguayan Judge Humberto Otazu complied with that request and said Mr. Peña will be held at a military base as investigations continue, in order to “guarantee his compliance” with the anti-corruption probe.
On Tuesday (November 3), regulators in Paraguay intervened in Ueno Bank, freezing the accounts of nearly three million customers and triggering a political crisis that led to Peña's removal by Congress on Friday (November 6) night.
Earlier on Saturday (November 7), Mr. Peña was questioned by prosecutors at the Attorney General's compound, in the capital Asuncion. The former President was not in handcuffs but was escorted by police.
Lawmakers accused Mr. Peña of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending. Mr. Peña has denied wrongdoing.
Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday (November 6) ordered the arrest of Mr. Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was transferred to a military base late Friday (November 6) as hundreds of protesters gathered outside his home.
The arrest order was issued soon after the Senate removed Mr. Peña from office in a unanimous vote. He was replaced by Vice-President Pedro Alliana, who began naming a new Cabinet on Saturday (November 7). The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received partial or full reimbursement of their deposits. Under Paraguayan law, deposits of up to $37,000 are insured.
Mr. Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday (November 5), but Congress did not accept it and pressed ahead with an impeachment trial. Opposition lawmakers insisted on his removal to prevent him from leaving office with immunity.
“He must go, but not home. He must go to a maximum-security prison,” opposition Sen Yolanda Paredes told reporters. “The public is fed up with impunity.”
In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm.
“I do not want my presence to be a cause of greater division or instability,” he wrote. “My responsibility is to put the country above my personal fate.”
Public outrage has intensified by the day. Thousands of protesters demanding access to their frozen savings and accountability for Ueno's failure have clashed with police firing rubber bullets and pepper spray this week. Paraguay's largest teachers' union, which has more than 40,000 members, plans to begin an indefinite national strike on Monday (November 9) to press for protection of public pension funds.
On Saturday (November 7), a few dozen protesters gathered outside the Attorney General's compound hoping to express their frustration with Mr. Peña, who was driven quickly out of the building.
Some of the protesters said they also want Paraguay's new President, who was a close ally of Mr. Peña, to be investigated.
“They are all accomplices,” said Liliana Jara, a demonstrator who showed up at the site. “They are part of the same clique.”

briefs.headline: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
briefs.deck: A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu
briefs.bodyText:
A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday (November 8, 2026), shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.
Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.
A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.
Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell down stairs while they were trying to flee.
The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m. local time, was located about 40 km below the Earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.
The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.
Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes.
Published - November 08, 2026 06:30 am IST

briefs.headline: 75+ Diwali messages, wishes and quotes to spread joy and light 2026
briefs.deck: Diwali is approaching, and many people will exchange festive greetings with family, friends, and colleagues. The article provides a variety of messages suitable for different recipients, including family, friends, and professional contacts. Short and humorous options are available for WhatsApp messages as well as heartfelt wishes for those living far away. It emphasizes conveying personal and…
briefs.bodyText:

stories.headline: Only one lane of KIA Road to be blocked for elevated corridor project in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Amid mounting criticism over traffic restrictions announced on the busy Ballari Road in the run-up to the Deepavali festive rush, Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) Saturday said only one lane on either side of the stretch will be barricaded for construction of the ambitious elevated corridor project. The remaining two lanes, along with service roads, will remain open to traffic moving towards Kempegowda International Airport.
The clarification comes after traffic police faced public fury over announcing traffic restrictions on one of the city’s busiest arterial roads without first ensuring that alternative routes leading to and from Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) are ready to absorb extra traffic load.
The Times of India
, in the report titled “No Escape: Alternative Roads Are In The Pits” published Saturday, had explained how alternative routes, including New BEL Road, Nagawara Road and RT Nagar Station Road, could lead to severe congestion without any improvement in the condition of carriageways.
Responding to the concerns, BDA chairperson NA Haris and commissioner P Manivannan, along with joint commissioner (traffic) Karthik Reddy and other police officers, conducted an inspection of the project corridor Saturday. 
They reviewed traffic conditions at Mehkri Circle and adjoining stretches.
Clarifying the extent of the proposed restrictions, Haris said construction activity will require barricading only one lane, measuring approximately 4.5m, on either side of the road. “Both sides of the road have three lanes each. Only one lane will be barricaded for construction. The remaining two lanes, along with the service road, will continue to be available for vehicular movement,” he said.
He directed officials and consultants to identify congestion-prone points and implement corrective measures to ensure smoother traffic movement during construction. He also stressed the need for better coordination between construction teams, traffic police and other agencies to minimise inconvenience to commuters.
“This project will be an invaluable asset to Bengaluru. Once completed in 18 months, an additional four-lane road will be available on this critical corridor, substantially easing traffic congestion. However, some public inconvenience during construction is inevitable. I urge citizens to cooperate and make necessary adjustments in the larger interest of the city,” Haris said.
Acknowledging the need to strengthen alternative routes, Haris said commuters could use New BEL Road and RT Nagar Station Road to avoid congestion on the project stretch. BDA plans to repair key roads connecting to Ballari Road, following suggestions from traffic police to ease congestion during the elevated corridor construction. The roads identified include BEL Road and Ganganagar–RT Nagar stretch. Reddy said: “Additional personnel will also be deployed near construction sites and on alternative routes to regulate traffic.”
The project involves the construction of a four-lane elevated corridor from UAS staff quarters to Mehkri Circle, alongside the proposed Hebbal tunnel works. The elevated corridor, estimated to cost Rs 445.7 crore, will cover 1.7km and is targeted for completion in 18 months.
Designed to ease congestion at Mekhri Circle, one of Bengaluru’s major traffic bottlenecks, the elevated structure will be supported by around 49 pillars and feature an elevated rotary junction. Two down-ramps are planned — one towards Yeshwantpur via CV Raman Road and another towards Jayamahal Road.
Two more signals to regulate traffic
Construction of the elevated corridor will require the demolition of two vehicular overpasses on the main carriageways. Their removal is expected to affect traffic flow not only on Ballari Road, but also on roads connecting nearby localities. Officials said two traffic signals will be installed after the overpasses are dismantled. Construction will then be taken up along the median while traffic continues on either side.
Widen road near Mehkri Circle: Cops
During the inspection, traffic police stressed the need to widen the road near Mehkri Circle to ease the existing bottleneck. The proposal requires the acquisition of 1.2 acres of defence land, an issue that has been pending for several years. Widening the existing road will help improve traffic flow towards both Jayamahal Road and Yeshwantpur. Haris said efforts are under way to secure the land from defence authorities. Chief minister D K Shivakumar had also taken up the matter with the defence ministry in the past, seeking its cooperation. Officials said Parachute Regiment Training Centre (PRTC) had agreed to part with its land, while discussions were under way with Directorate General of Quality Assurance (DGQA) to secure the remaining land.
Will BDA stick to 18-month deadline?
On whether the elevated corridor could be completed within the stipulated 18 months, given BDA’s track record of delays in executing projects, Haris expressed confidence that the deadline will be met. “This will be a new road infrastructure facility for Bengaluru, aimed at easing congestion between Esteem Mall and Mehkri Circle. Construction will have an impact on traffic, but measures will be taken to minimise inconvenience to commuters. We are not banning public transport (including BMTC/KSRTC and private buses) or private vehicles on this road, only goods vehicles will be diverted,” he said.

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s GBA launches phase 2 of ‘Ward One’
stories.bodyText:
Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Saturday directed officials to prepare a comprehensive plan for the redevelopment of the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction. The plan should focus on pedestrian safety, public transport integration and smoother traffic movement, he said.
The directions came during the launch of the second phase of the ‘Ward One’ campaign. The second phase has been launched across around 40 wards. The first phase covered 43 wards, with nearly 90% of the identified works completed, Mr. Gowda said.
On Saturday, the Minister inspected the K.R. Puram-Tin Factory Junction and reviewed the problems from ongoing metro and K-RIDE works and the pedestrian infrastructure, following which directions were issued.
The plan would be prepared jointly by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), Namma Metro officials, and Janaagraha, he said. The plan would cover road design, footpaths, bus bays, bus stops and traffic management. The Minister also called for scientifically redesigning the junction, improving road curves, and providing free left turns wherever necessary.
He directed metro officials to restore roads affected by the construction without delay. “Potholes on connecting roads must be repaired within a week. Roads at lower levels, which are prone to flooding, also need to be improved,” he told officials.
The campaign brings together various civic agencies to address potholes, damaged footpaths, garbage accumulation, construction waste, streetlights and drain desilting.

stories.headline: I PU question papers to be set at State level in Karnataka
stories.bodyText:
To improve the quality of Pre-University (PU) education, the Department of School Education has decided to prepare the question papers for the I PU annual examinations at the State level from the current academic year.
The question papers will be prepared by the Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board. However, the examinations will be conducted under the supervision of the Department of School Education (Pre-University). The State government issued an order to this effect on Saturday.
A uniform examination timetable applicable to all PU colleges across the State will be prepared for the conduct of these examinations. On the day of the examination, the question papers will be transmitted to the colleges in a digital format.
Only the practical examinations for I PU will be conducted according to a schedule prepared at the district level. Although the question papers will be prepared at the State level, the evaluation process will continue to take place at the college level. The results will be published only after they have been reviewed and approved by the respective Deputy Director Pre-University of the district.
The order stated that it would also pave the way for improving the pass percentage in the II PU.

briefs.headline: Master plan on cards to transform Tin Factory junction in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 One of Bengaluru’s most notorious traffic bottlenecks, KR Pura Tin Factory Junction, could finally be in line for a comprehensive makeover, with Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda directing officials to prepare a master plan for its holistic redevelopment.
During an inspection of the junction Saturday as part of the second phase of the Ward One campaign, the minister instructed officials to draw up a people-centric and pedestrian-friendly plan that addresses traffic movement, public transport integration, footpaths, road geometry and commuter convenience.
The junction serves as a critical gateway connecting KR Pura with Whitefield, ITPL, Marathahalli and the city’s eastern suburbs while also handling traffic entering Bengaluru from the outskirts. The convergence of multiple traffic streams, ongoing Metro construction and increasing commuter volumes have made it one of the city’s most congested intersections.
The minister also stressed the need to improve pedestrian connectivity around the junction, especially for commuters shifting between different modes of transport. Road widening, scientific redesign of traffic movements and provision of free-left turns wherever feasible should also be incorporated into the plan, he said.
Calling for coordinated action, Byre Gowda directed GBA, BMRCL and other stakeholders to jointly prepare the master plan. Urban planning organisations Janaagraha and Agra Indians have also been asked to contribute.
He expressed concern over the condition of roads around the junction, many of which have been damaged due to ongoing Metro and K-Ride works. Officials were instructed to ensure that roads are restored immediately after civil works are completed.
According to Byre Gowda, around 90% of the works across 43 wards identified in the first phase of the the Ward One campaign have already been completed, while the second phase has now been launched in around 40 wards across the city.
Ward One Drive by numbers
1,035 potholes filled across Bengaluru
564 black spots cleared
598 tonnes of garbage removed from black spots
1,542 debris dumps cleared, with 1,965 tonnes of debris removed
52.7km of footpaths repaired
720 encroachments removed from footpaths
57 junctions improved
56.8km of roadside drains and 10.2km of stormwater drains desilted
300 new streetlights installed and 783 streetlights repaired
300 public complaints resolved on the spot
Political Sparring Overshadows Civic Drive
A routine civic inspection at Tin Factory Junction briefly turned political after supporters of the BJP and Congress started making accusations over development works in the KR Pura constituency. The exchange escalated into a verbal spat involving BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj and former Congress MLC Narayanaswamy, with both sides arguing over road conditions and utilisation of development funds. While Basavaraj alleged that residents raising civic concerns were being targeted, Krishna Byre Gowda said political differences should not distract from the larger goal of addressing public infrastructure issues.

briefs.headline: This Deepavali, let there be light: Can Bengaluru celebrate without the noise?
briefs.bodyText:
Actor Dia Mirza didn’t expect a political storm to erupt from a short video. But her pollution-awareness message has triggered a nationwide debate on a cracker-free Deepavali. The city has been given a two-hour window for bursting crackers, but residents are asking whether celebration should come at the cost of those who cannot escape the noise.
Pet parents and environmentalists are urging the city to embrace a more mindful Deepavali — one where the glow of diyas outshines the din, and the festivities bring joy without causing distress.
A little less boom for pets, elders and sensitive ears
Sudden, loud bursts can leave pets trembling, hiding or on high alert. For senior citizens, noise and smoke can disrupt sleep and aggravate breathing difficulties. Neurodivergent children and adults can also find the sensory overload distressing.
“My pets’ favourite time of day is the evening on the balcony, except during Deepavali. They get anxious and flinch at every nearby cracker burst,” says a psychology student. Closing the windows to keep out the smoke and noise, he says, “does little good”.
The cost of a loud night
Raghav Joshi, a 25-year-old charter pilot, says his three-year-old Great Dane, Master Obi Wan, is “terrified” of firecrackers.
“It always breaks my heart. It seems like it takes years of life off him to live through it,” he says.
Calling late-night bursting “downright masochistic”, Raghav believes some people continue to participate simply because it has become an established tradition. “They pretend to like it because it is an established tradition,” he says.
Environmentalists say individual restraint must be backed by stricter enforcement. Urban strategist Vinod Jacob calls for substantial fines and, where legally permissible, imprisonment for repeat offenders.
“We must strictly protect the hours between 10 pm and 6 am from firecracker noise, with particular consideration for seniors, children, animals and neurodivergent people,” he says. “Responsible celebration means respecting everyone’s right to peace, well-being and clean air.”
A greener Diwali: Celebrating without fireworks
Not everyone opposed to crackers believes in campaigning against them. "I don’t burst crackers, and I hate the loud noises and pollution. But I don’t go around preaching about it either,” says a Bengaluru resident. Pointing out that firecrackers are not the sole cause of the country's air pollution, the resident adds, “Me saying anything won’t stop people from bursting them. So I wear my earplugs and mask and stay inside as much as possible during Deepavali.”
The frustration is also evident on online forums. 
A Kumaraswamy Layout
 resident, posting on Reddit, described people bursting bijli crackers while walking down a residential road at 11 pm, followed by another minute-long burst nearby.
“I find it appalling that people can be so inconsiderate,” the user wrote, adding that no amount of police patrolling would help curb the practice.
For some, the cost of green crackers is another deterrent. One Reddit user complained about paying ₹400 for a packet of phooljharis, while another said they preferred spending the money on sweets, fairy lights and gifts instead of crackers.
Highlight box
8 pm to 10 pm: Bengaluru’s cracker window
The Karnataka government has restricted firecracker bursting to 8 pm–10 pm during Deepavali, in line with Supreme Court guidelines on noise and air pollution. “This will be the only period during which bursting of crackers will be permitted,” said Forest, Environment and Ecology Minister Ramalinga Reddy.

briefs.headline: Karnataka minister UT Khader orders end to plain-paper prescriptions at government hospitals
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Health minister UT Khader has directed officials to immediately stop doctors at govt hospitals from prescribing medicines on plain paper and asking patients to buy them from private medical stores. He warned that doctors and officials found violating rules will face strict action, while pharmacies accepting such prescriptions risk losing their licences.
The directions follow a Vijaya Karnataka reality check published on Nov 6, which exposed the practice of doctors issuing prescriptions on plain paper, commonly referred to as ‘white slips’, and directing patients to private medical stores. The report highlighted how a practice that bypasses official hospital prescriptions has been affecting patients who approach govt facilities expecting free medicines.
Responding
to
 the report, Khader said, “Poor patients coming to govt hospitals must receive free, quality medicines at the hospital itself. Writing prescriptions on plain paper and allowing sale of medicines through outside medical stores without authorisation will not be permitted.”

briefs.headline: ‘Looting non-residents’: Bengaluru Malayalis furious after steep insurance premium hike
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Thousands of Keralites in the city are up in arms over a steep hike in premiums under the Keralam govt’s health insurance scheme for non-residents. Last Tuesday, 12 Malayali associations staged a protest outside the Non-Resident Keralites Affairs (Norka) office on Infantry Road, demanding a rollback.
Norka Care, a digital health insurance initiative for non-resident Keralites (NRKs), was announced in Sept 2025 and became operational in Nov of that year. It combines group medical insurance and group personal accident coverage. Thousands of Malayalis across India and abroad enrolled, attracted by coverage ranging from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 1 crore and annual premiums starting at Rs 8,101 for individuals and Rs 13,411 for families.
Norka claims the scheme recorded a 99.5% claim settlement ratio within a year, the highest in the country. However, from Nov 2026, premiums will be linked to the policyholder’s age, with senior citizens facing the steepest increase.
A person aged 51-60 will now have to pay Rs 35,664 annually to insure their family, while those in the 61-70 age group will pay Rs 48,718. A joint committee of Bengaluru Malayali organisations said premiums for families with policyholders above the age of 41 have increased two to seven times. 
“The hike is equivalent to looting hardworking migrant Malayalis. Govt has hiked premiums for other policies as well, even though the Rs 5 lakh claim policy has many members,” the committee said.
Jojo PJ, president of Bengaluru Malayali Forum, urged Keralam chief minister VD Satheesan to exempt existing members from the hike and allow them to renew at the same premium. He also sought their inclusion in the newly announced Oommen Chandy health insurance scheme.
Jojo, who has been a Bengaluru resident for over three decades, alleged that welfare schemes for non-resident Keralites were being changed based on political grounds.
Aswathy Raveendran, a Bannerghatta resident, said she had switched to Norka Care because of its low premiums and wide coverage. She persuaded around five other families to do the same. “The Norka Care scheme was very attractive as it offered good coverage for very little premium, which made me quit the previous policy which I had.”
Vibin Krishnan, a professor enrolled in the scheme, questioned its transparency, saying private insurers now offered better clarity on benefits.
When 
TOI
 contacted the Norka-Roots satellite office in Bengaluru, officials declined to comment. City-based Malayali organisations have sought Satheesan’s urgent intervention.

briefs.headline: Karnataka MBBS counselling: 109 new students register for vacant seats
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has received 109 new registrations for a special counselling round to fill 191 MBBS seats left vacant in the state after all previous rounds. In all, 153 students have entered options.
The Medical Counselling Committee announced the special schedule after 2,000 seats remained vacant across India. KEA allowed candidates who had not registered earlier to apply online and participate.
Candidates who have not been allotted a medical seat are eligible, while those allotted dental seats can participate only for medical seats. Students must pay a caution deposit of Rs 25 lakh for medical seats and Rs 1 lakh for dental seats.
Mithesh Kumar Moodukonaje, founder of National PU Students, Parents and Teachers’ Association, said colleges have stopped sharply reducing fees after doing so during the final days of the previous round. He said lower-tier colleges were charging Rs 65 lakh to Rs 75 lakh, while top-tier colleges were quoting Rs 85 lakh to Rs 1 crore for seats.
A medical college owner with 10 vacant seats on the KEA list said students who had planned to take a gap year and repeat National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test were reconsidering admission if the fees were affordable.
According to KEA, Srinivasa Institute of Medical Research Centre, Mangaluru, has the most vacancies at 32, followed by PES University Institute of Medical Sciences and Research with 26 and Sri Chamundeshwari Medical College Hospital & Research Institute with 21. Bagalkot Medical College and Research Institute has 14 vacant seats.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s grinding stone horror: Bereaved families want death sentence for the killer of 7
briefs.deck: Families of the seven murder victims in Bengaluru are demanding capital punishment for accused Indushekhar. The brutal nature of the crimes has devastated the relatives, who seek justice for their loved ones. One victim’s mother expressed her anguish, stating her daughter did nothing to deserve such violence. A relative raised concerns about the surviving child, who will suffer these traumatic…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The anguish and grief of the families of the seven serial murder victims in the city have given way to anger, with one demand echoing among the bereaved relatives: alleged killer Indushekhar must be hanged for the brutal killings. The manner in which the victims were allegedly lured and killed has further compounded the trauma of their kin.
Amid the pall of gloom, Kumar, a close relative of the victims and maternal uncle of the murdered 
Nalini
, told TOI the sheer brutality of the crime was beyond comprehension. He said the accused had shown no mercy even to a seven-year-old boy, who had done nothing to invite such cruelty.
“What kind of cold-blooded murders are these? He didn’t even spare a seven-year-old child who had absolutely nothing to do with his alleged vengeance. The victims were called separately for dinner and then bludgeoned to death with a grinding stone while they were asleep. What is even more disturbing is that he allegedly made his own daughter assist him in committing this heinous crime. It is good that police have arrested him, but we want him to be hanged for what he has done. His senseless act of vengeance has destroyed 3-4 families,” Kumar said.
He also expressed concern for the 10-year-old boy who managed to escape from the clutches of Indushekhar and his daughter. 
“The boy will have to carry these painful memories for the rest of his life. Every day, he will be reminded of how his parents and other family members were killed. No child should have to endure such a nightmare,” he said.
Tungamma, Nalini’s mother and the complainant in the case, questioned why the accused had targeted her daughter. “What had my daughter done to him? She never spoke to or interacted with him. Only on a few occasions, when Indushekhar came for dinner, would she speak to him and ask what he wanted. A few days ago, Nalini told me that Indushekhar was seen fighting with Sunitha and Rupavathi over domestic issues. I had asked her to stay away from such fights as she was not involved. She never spoke ill of him or insulted him. Yet, he decided to kill her.... When police told me in detail what happened, I fainted. Yes, he should be hanged,” she said.
N Venugopal, another relative of Tungamma, expressed concern over her health. “Since the news broke, we’ve been with Tungamma and the others. She refuses to eat or drink water. She repeatedly asks me to take her to the place where her daughter’s body was dumped. I tried to explain that even police have not found Nalini’s body yet... I knew Nalini since she was a child, and it is horrifying that she was killed in such an inhumane manner. I had also seen her son, the 10-year-old boy who fortunately escaped. Now, who will look after him? Tungamma is elderly and cannot care for him the way his parents did,” he said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Police Complaints Authority member proposes seniority badges for police personnel
briefs.deck: If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel
briefs.bodyText:
A member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority has urged the State government to introduce special designations and insignia on police uniforms to recognise the seniority of personnel based on their years of service, irrespective of promotions.
In a letter dated November 5 to the Minister for Home, IT-BT and e-Governance, Priyank Kharge, Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority (KSPCA) member Mohan Kumar Danappa has proposed introducing three categories of seniority for police personnel, from constables to non-IPS officers.
According to his proposal, personnel completing five years of service should be designated as “senior”, those completing 10 years as “super senior”, and those completing 15 years as “most senior”. He suggested that distinct insignia corresponding to these designations be displayed on the right side of the chest, above the nameplate.
Mr. Danappa pointed out that although police personnel generally become eligible for promotion after five years of service, promotions were largely dependent on the availability of vacancies. As a result, many experienced personnel remained in the same rank for years without any formal recognition of their seniority and experience.
He said the proposed system would recognise their long service, enhance their sense of responsibility and ensure that experienced personnel receive due respect within the department and society.
Citing the practice of providing black collar patches to IPS officers after 10 years of service, he said similar arrangements were also followed in certain State police forces and Central Armed Police Forces.
He also referred to the State government’s recent initiatives to replace British-era police caps and introduce lanyards in place of whistle chains, stating that recognising seniority through uniform insignia would be another significant reform to boost the morale of police personnel.
If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel, he said.
Mr. Danappa has requested the Home Minister to examine the proposal and to issue necessary directions to the authorities concerned for its implementation.

briefs.headline: Karnataka dairy farmers seek KMF reforms based on Amul model, more investment in milk procurement
briefs.deck: Farmers demand that the State government improve animal health, vaccination, artificial insemination and breed improvement facilities at the village level, as a majority of the farmers involved in dairy farming are in rural areas
briefs.bodyText:
Following the recent hike in the prices of milk, curd and their by-products, farmers put forward a series of demands to the State government and the Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF). These included action against hotels for disproportionately increasing the prices of tea, coffee and other food items.
They also demanded that milk and curd be included in the food security basket for distribution to children at anganwadis, KMF’s financial position be strengthened, and the federation be run along the lines of the Amul model with minimal political interference.
Badagalapur Nagendra, president, Bengaluru, Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, said, “Investment should be increased in the collection of milk, refrigeration, processing and value addition. Our State farmers involved in animal husbandry and farming have the potential to provide more than one crore litres of milk, and the KMF must work towards utilising this potential. However, this can happen only when the system is strengthened financially and is free from political interference — as in the Amul model. Fair elections must be conducted in the KMF so that elected candidates don’t have vested interests.”
He added, “The Amul model is stronger when it comes to marketing strategy, building infrastructure and marking its presence in other States so that it benefits their farmer community.”
Besides this, the farmers also demanded that the State government improve animal health, vaccination, artificial insemination and breed improvement facilities at the village level, as a majority of the farmers involved in dairy farming were in rural areas. “Improving all these facilities at the village level will lead to an increase in the milk yield. Similar to insurance for crop failure, appropriate insurance should be provided for cows and buffaloes.”
Highlighting the drought conditions in the State and the shortage of fodder, he said, “At present, cattle feed is provided by the KMF, but the quality should be enhanced, and it must be provided at an affordable price. Local fodder production should be encouraged by providing high-yielding seeds at the gram panchayat level to farmers, especially during droughts. A system should be developed to use maize, which is produced in large quantities in Karnataka, for animal feed at low prices.”
Include milk in food basket
Meanwhile, T.N. Prakash Kammarady, professor of Agricultural Economics, University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (UAS-B), emphasised that the government has to provide milk and curd to children in anganwadis. He said, “Along with cereals, milk and curd should be made part of the nutritious food basket under the National Food Security Act. These should be provided by local cooperative milk unions through midday meals, especially at anganwadis to support women and child nutrition programmes.”
Mr. Kammarady urged the government to crack down on hotels for disproportionately increasing the prices of tea and coffee. “With one litre of milk, around 20 cups of coffee and tea can be made, whether at home or in hotels. They will add sufficient water to it also. However, increasing the prices from ₹20 to ₹30 per cup is not justified. It is a daylight loot of customers, just because they will come for a sip of tea or coffee. The government should crack down and regulate the prices of food items in hotels that are being increased in the name of the price hike,” he said.
MSP for milk
While approving the government’s milk price hike to support farmers, farmer groups have urged the government to determine the overall cost of producing milk and have requested that a fair purchase price be fixed according to the Swaminathan Commission’s C2+50% principle. This principle is a methodology to determine the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for agricultural crops, under which the MSP is set at a minimum of a 50% profit margin over the comprehensive cost of production.
Import protection
Mr. Nagendra also urged the State government to work with the Centre to restrict imports of foreign dairy products and protect domestic farmers, particularly in view of the recent trade agreements with the U.S., the European Union and New Zealand. Citing the subsidies and support extended to dairy farmers in these countries, he stressed the need for safeguards to protect Karnataka’s dairy farmers and cooperatives such as the KMF from possible import liberalisation.

stories.headline: Samvat 2083 outlook: Stocks, sectors and levels investors should keep an eye on
stories.deck: As the festive season of Diwali draws near, investors are keenly eyeing the future of Dalal Street for the forthcoming Samvat 2083. According to Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, attention should be given to high-quality stocks while keeping a diversified portfolio. Despite global uncertainties, the domestic growth outlook in India looks promising, which is beneficial for corporate profits.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Diwali is here, and investors are looking ahead to Samvat 2083 with one key question: what lies ahead for Dalal Street in the new year? While India's domestic growth outlook remains encouraging, global uncertainties and market volatility could keep investors on their toes. Market participants are therefore advising investors to be selective with their stock choices and keep their return expectations realistic.
Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund expects moderate returns from equities in the coming Samvat. In its annual 'Muhurat Picks Samvat 2083' presentation, the fund house advised investors to focus on quality companies, maintain a balanced portfolio and stay invested for the long term rather than chase short-term market rallies.
It also cautioned that geopolitical tensions, changes in crude oil prices and the cautious approach of global central banks could keep markets volatile over the coming year. A long-term investment approach, it said, would help investors navigate these uncertainties.
India's growth outlook remains encouraging
Despite global concerns, India's domestic growth outlook remains positive. Kotak Mutual Fund expects the country's GDP to grow 7.1% in FY27, with domestic demand continuing to support corporate earnings. 
High-frequency indicators also point to a broad-based economic recovery.
However, the fund house believes investors should not expect exceptionally high equity returns in the new Samvat. Moderate returns, it said, are a more realistic expectation for the broader market.
There is also some valuation comfort in large-cap and mid-cap stocks. According to Kotak Mutual Fund's presentation, major market indices were trading below their long-term average valuations as of October 31, 2026.
This comes after an uneven performance across equity market segments since the previous Diwali. Data covering October 20, 2025, to October 31, 2026, showed divergent movements in the Nifty 50 TRI, Nifty Midcap 150 TRI and Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks experiencing sharper volatility during the period.
Meanwhile, analysts at domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOSL) said Nifty valuations were attractive at 17.5 times forward earnings, around 16% below the long-term average. Small-cap stocks, however, continued to trade at a 25% premium to their historical average.
The brokerage expects earnings growth to recover over the coming years. Nifty earnings per share are projected to rise 16% and 14% year-on-year in FY27 and FY28, respectively, compared with 5% in FY26.
Which sectors could offer opportunities in Samvat 2083?
For the new Samvat, market experts favour banking and financial services, capital markets, manufacturing, global outsourcing and exports, consumption and digital businesses.
They also see opportunities in healthcare devices, aerospace, auto components, pharmaceutical ingredients, garments, port cargo, organised jewellery and quick-commerce platforms.
Against this backdrop, Kotak Mutual Fund's investment strategy centres on identifying quality companies and maintaining disciplined asset allocation. The fund house has advised investors to remain focused on their long-term investment goals instead of trying to benefit from short-term market movements.
It has also recommended that investors align their mutual fund choices with their individual risk profiles and seek guidance from financial advisors before making investment decisions.
Muhurat trading: Why experts advise a cautious approach
As investors prepare for the special Diwali trading session on Sunday, market experts have called for a cautious, stock-specific approach. With benchmark indices approaching key resistance levels, limited liquidity during the session could amplify market movements, they said.
Muhurat trading is traditionally considered an auspicious occasion to begin investments and review financial portfolios. However, experts have cautioned investors against making impulsive decisions driven by festive sentiment. Instead, they have advised them to focus on company fundamentals, valuations and long-term financial goals.
The approach, experts said, should differ depending on the investment horizon. Long-term investors can use the occasion to review their asset allocation and selectively accumulate fundamentally strong stocks. Short-term traders, meanwhile, should monitor technical levels and global cues before taking positions.
For those entering the stock market for the first time, experts recommend starting with small investments in fundamentally strong companies and adopting a long-term holding approach. They have also advised against buying stocks simply because the occasion is considered auspicious.
Given the possibility of lower liquidity during the limited trading session, investors should avoid placing large orders or trading aggressively, experts added.
Nifty support and resistance levels to watch
The cautious approach also comes as both benchmark indices approach crucial resistance zones following a recent rally. Market experts expect trading to remain sideways to consolidative during the Muhurat session.
Trading around 24,600, Nifty has immediate support at 24,350, while resistance is placed in the 24,700-24,800 range.
Experts have also flagged the possibility of profit booking after six consecutive sessions of gains. Geopolitical concerns, crude oil volatility and weakness in global markets could add to the pressure.
As Samvat 2083 begins, the broader advice for investors is to keep return expectations realistic, remain selective with stock choices and stick to disciplined investment strategies rather than get carried away by short-term market movements.

stories.headline: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
stories.deck: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility
stories.bodyText:
From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.
For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%.
