stories.headline: ‘Loads more ahead’: British High Commission in India hails trade deal amid Diwali celebrations
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The British High Commission in India marked Diwali by highlighting the landmark India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA), saying the deal has given the two countries more reasons to celebrate and expressing optimism about the future of their partnership.
In a post on X, the High Commission said this year’s Diwali celebrations were especially bright following the delivery of the trade agreement.
"The Diwali smiles are extra bright at this year! With our landmark Free Trade Agreement delivered and loads more ahead for the modern UK-India partnership, we had loads to celebrate. HappyDiwali to everyone celebrating!" the British High Commission in India said.
The celebrations come after the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) came into effect in July, marking a step towards closer trade and investment ties between the two countries.
The agreement aims to expand economic ties through improved market access, trade liberalisation and tariff concessions.
Under the deal, nearly 99% of Indian exports will receive zero-duty access to the UK, covering almost 100% of their trade value. It is expected to improve the competitiveness of Indian exports, boost bilateral trade and investment, and create opportunities for businesses.
The agreement also includes one of the most ambitious commitments on services that the UK has offered under a free trade agreement.
Several foreign diplomatic missions in India also celebrated Diwali with their staff, sharing glimpses of the festivities on social media.
Japan’s Ambassador to India, Ono Keiichi, celebrated the festival with Indian and Japanese colleagues at the Embassy of Japan. The occasion marked his third Diwali in the country.
Sharing a video of the celebrations, Ono said celebrating with embassy staff had made the festival even more memorable. The video showed traditional diyas, colourful rangoli designs and marigold decorations, with employees dressed in traditional Indian attire.
"Celebrated Diwali with all the Embassy staff! Sharing the joy of this beautiful festival with both Indian and Japanese colleagues made my 3rd Diwali in India even more memorable. Happy Diwali!!" ONO Keiichi wrote.
The French Embassy in India also shared a video of its annual Diwali celebrations, featuring embassy staff and French Ambassador to India Thierry Mathou.
Posted on X on Friday, the 93-second video showed employees preparing for the festival before the ceremonial lighting of a brass diya decorated with marigold flowers. Mathou was also seen lighting the lamp and extending greetings.
"Diwali is a beautiful celebration of life, hope and new beginnings. May this festival bring joy to every home and continue to strengthen the bonds of friendship between France and India," he added.

briefs.headline: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
briefs.deck: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments
briefs.bodyText:
What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).
Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.
For a few weeks, Rampur, on the banks of the Sutlej river, comes alive with the fair (November 11-14 this year, with trading grounds open through the month), offering a sensory map of the Himalaya. Colourful textiles, yak wool, pashmina, dry fruits, agricultural produce, Kinnauri apples, indigenous crafts and precious stones fill the marketplace. Among its most captivating sights are the magnificent Chamurthi horses, the hardy “ships of the cold desert”.
Touch of royalty
Traders once travelled from Tibet, Nepal, Central Asia and Afghanistan. Tradition traces the fair’s origins to a 17th-century treaty between Raja Kehri Singh of Bushahr and Tibet, establishing it as a meeting point for traders, pilgrims and storytellers along the Silk Route. Though trans-Himalayan trade declined after Tibet’s occupation in 1959, the fair survived on the Buddhist circuit and was accorded international status by the Himachal Pradesh government.
Pratibha Singh, a member of the Rampur Bushahr royal family which founded the fair and continues to honour the tradition, recalls its legacy of pashmina and Kinnauri shawls, some woven over years, alongside trans-Himalayan textiles and local produce. The GI-tagged Kinnauri shawl, with bright geometric motifs, speaks its own language of colour: white for water, yellow for earth, red for fire, green for air, and blue for sky.
On my last visit, a group of elderly women from South India told me they discovered the fair through a fellow traveller whose husband was a biker in the 1990s. A friend from Odisha recalls how in the 90s, his ophthalmologist-father’s eye camps in Rampur led to lifelong friendships and an annual habit of sourcing Kinnauri apples and dry fruits.
From barter to digital payments
For Ami Chand Gautam, a Lavi trader since the 1980s, the fair tells a story of changing prices and livelihoods. He remembers when “chilgoza, the rare pine nut gathered in Kinnaur’s upper reaches, sold for just ₹4-₹5 per kg, almost the price of rice then. Today, it fetches ₹14,000-15,000 per kg,” he says.
“Who could have imagined that?” quips Gautam, for whom Lavi is more than a marketplace, where mountain wealth (wool, pashmina, livestock and dry fruits) was once exchanged for plains produce (salt, jaggery, grains, cloth, etc.). Traders now accept online payments and use courier services.
The food reflects the fair’s evolving palate. Last year, I saw steaming siddu, kodra (millet) roti, moodie (millet trail mix), momo, and desi mithai being sold alongsidechow mein, golgappa, chaat, and dosa.
According to Rampur sub-divisional magistrate Harsh Amarendra Singh, “Lavi generates approx. ₹2.5 crore annually through plot and stall instalments, against an overall expenditure of nearly ₹2 crore. About 70% of the expenditure is allocated to local artists and cultural programmes. The government’s efforts aim to strengthen the fair’s identity as one of India’s most distinctive cultural and artisan mountain fairs.”
Atma Ram Kedarta, a retired officer who’s seen the fair since his childhood in the 1950s and later headed its cultural committee, remembers how “cultural evenings became one of Lavi’s biggest attractions”. However, he says, “The government should ensure local artists are paid a fair and decent fee. There is a significant gap between what is paid to Himachali artists and performers from outside.”
I realised Lavi’s heartbeat is its women as I watched them run stalls, negotiate deals, manage businesses, and lead cultural traditions. Self-help groups have further empowered small-scale women entrepreneurs.
How to reach
Custodians of tradition
The fair helped traders from the lower hills and northern plains settle in Rampur. “Nearly 75% of Rampur’s businessmen are migrants who settled generations ago,” says Kedarta. Harbans Kumar came from Punjab in the 1950s, recognising its business potential. Today, his grandson Sarthak continues the family trade. Calling himself “more Pahari than Punjabi”, he grew up “speaking the local language and dancing the folk Nati” and says, “Himachal isn’t just where my family trades, this is my home.”
“A fair is always for the children,” quips Anupam Kashyap, deputy commissioner of Shimla. The administration has introduced essay competition in schools, with prizes of ₹10,000-25,000, encouraging children to “speak to local elders, their grandparents, traders, travellers and community members, to learn about Lavi’s lived history”. “The next generation will be the keeper of Lavi’s grand past, the flagbearer of its present, and the custodian of its future,” Kashyap concludes.
The Noida-based writer is a chef and culinary researcher.

briefs.headline: Automation has boosted employment, hiring of low-skilled workers in India, says ABB chief
briefs.deck: ABB India has committed to invest $75 million in India over 2026 and 2027 to fuel its organic expansion in the country, with a new focus on Tier-II and Tier-III cities
briefs.bodyText:
Contrary to fears that automation will lead to job losses, especially among lower-skilled workers, high-precision engineering firm ABB India has found that automation has not only allowed it to substantially increase its workforce in India, but also to employ lower-skilled workers and train them, the company’s CEO and managing director Sanjeev Sharma said in an interview.
Further, the company has committed to invest $75 million (around ₹708 crore) in India over 2026 and 2027 to fuel its organic expansion in the country, with a new focus on Tier-II and Tier-III cities, ABB India’s managing director-designate T. K. Sridhar said during the joint interview. Mr. Sridhar will take over as managing director in January 2027.
The need for lower skills
“It’s been a very interesting change with technology,” Mr. Sharma said at the company’s headquarters in Bengaluru. “If you look at our plant in Nelamangala (Bengaluru), where we manufacture switchgear, it’s a fully automated operation with a lot of robotics and very young people working on the desk to manufacture.”
“In the same factory, a few years ago when we hadn’t done that much automation, we required very skilled people,” he added. “But now, with automation and the guiding screens in front of each operator, we are able to bring very young people and train them very quickly to perform that complex job.”
Mr. Sharma explained that, with enhanced automation in ABB’s factories, the need for skilled labour has actually gone down. He added that while a worker’s departure used to delay hiring a replacement due to the need for skilled workers, that delay has now substantially reduced.
“Most of them are youngsters, young girls,” Mr. Sharma said. “Even if you are using a screwdriver, the screwdriver has sensors, it knows exactly how much torque to use. So, the device will move only if you put in the right torque.
“There are interlocks so that you are sure of the quality, but at the same time, the younger people with relatively less skills are able to be deployed,” he added.
He also explained that the speed and precision enabled by automation have helped the company to grow its operations in India and thereby also increase its employment. ABB India saw its employment grow 57% from around 7,000 workers in 2021 to more than 11,000 in 2026.
Investing in India’s hinterland
According to the company’s data, its revenue has nearly doubled to around $1.4 billion in 2025 from $730 million in 2021. Further, about 88% of its business comes from within India, and 12% from exports.
Of the $75 million the company has committed to invest over 2026 and 2027, $22 million will go to its Nashik electrification plant, $21 million to its motion plant in Peenya in Bengaluru, $14 million to its electrification and automation plants in Nelamangala, $12 million in its electrification research and development lab and office in Hyderabad, and $6 million in its motion plant in Vadodara.
“On average, over the last 5-6 years, our capital expenditure has been ₹300 crore in India every year,” Mr. Sridhar said. “I think that investment journey will continue, because you need to build factories as the demand is robust. So, we keep modernising our factories.”
“Organic expansion is very interesting for us because it definitely gives us better return on investment,” he added. “We believe that is a journey that will continue.”
Mr. Sridhar added that the company has also changed its focus to also look at Tier-II and Tier-III cities in India.
“When we started this journey 8-10 years ago, we saw that we were all focused on customers in the bigger metros,” he explained. “Even our sales offices were structured around that. Then we realized that the future market is not going to stay there but is going to spread across the other parts of the country, so then we created cluster offices, which were more interesting to address the hinterlands of India.”
What is driving this, he said, was the rise of industries in smaller cities.
“I think there’s a new age of entrepreneurs who have started to build their own capacity over there and go into the industries and that’s helping us grow in these areas,” Mr. Sridhar said.
(The author was in Bengaluru at the invitation of ABB India)

briefs.headline: As AI stocks correct, Goldman Sachs sees opportunity in healthcare & non-AI equities
briefs.deck: US midterm elections could shift market dynamics, prompting investors to adopt more defensive positions in their portfolios. Healthcare is anticipated to benefit from advancements in AI as it sees potential growth. Many traditional defensive sectors, however, appear less attractive due to elevated valuations. Goldman Sachs emphasizes the importance of focusing on companies with strong…
briefs.bodyText:
The US midterm elections could accelerate the ongoing rotation in stock markets, with healthcare emerging as a potential defensive investment amid a correction in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks, according to Lou Miller, global head of custom basket trading at Goldman Sachs.
Speaking on Goldman Sachs' The Markets podcast, Miller said investors had already started moving towards defensive positions ahead of the elections, amid a challenging environment for active investors in the second half of 2026.
"We've seen people get very defensive. If you look at beta-adjusted net exposure in our prime book, it's definitely at very low levels versus history," he said.
Miller pointed to sharp declines in several segments of the AI investment theme. Data centre stocks have fallen 36% from their highs earlier this year, while memory stocks have declined 42%, optical networking stocks 46% and NeoCloud stocks 57%.
However, he said the correction had lowered expectations and could leave room for positive surprises.
"I think the silver lining is the bar is much, much lower for surprises and there are positive catalysts ahead," he said.
"The multiple for the data centre trade is about half of what it was in June," Miller added, saying valuations had moved to healthier levels.
Healthcare emerges as potential AI growth area
Miller identified healthcare as a possible beneficiary of the next phase of AI adoption, saying the sector could be among the few to see accelerating earnings growth next year.
"I think the next leg of the AI trade is actually healthcare, and I think that's also a very defensive sector that historically is very uncorrelated to AI," he said.
He noted that healthcare companies were increasingly adopting AI in areas such as medical tools and diagnostics, with the sector moving from challenges towards growth opportunities.
Miller, however, cautioned against treating traditional defensive sectors such as consumer staples as automatically attractive, arguing that elevated valuations had reduced their appeal.
"Expensive defensives I don't think are defensive," he said.
He suggested investors focus on companies with strong balance sheets, quality earnings and healthy free cash flows.
Goldman Sachs executive outlines market outlook
Outlining his preferred investment strategy, Miller said: "I think the S&P 500 excluding AI is the trade."
He cited attractive valuations and earnings growth prospects as reasons for his preference.
Looking ahead, Miller identified employment, inflation, corporate earnings and the US Federal Reserve's December 9 policy decision as key factors that could influence markets.
On the outlook for US stocks towards the end of the year, he expressed cautious optimism, anticipating a modest rally that he described as a "relaxed Santa Rally".

briefs.headline: Coca-Cola's Indian bottling business files for IPO; 99.75 crore shares up for sale
briefs.deck: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd has filed its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India. The planned IPO will involve the sale of up to 99.75 crore equity shares by the promoter. Coca-Cola aims to list HCCH by 2027 amid a global asset-light strategy for its bottling assets. The company operates through 14 bottling plants across India and has a significant distribution…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Coca-Cola Company's Indian bottling business, Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), has initiated the process for a stock market listing by filing its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi).
The proposed 
initial public offering
 (IPO) will involve the sale of up to 99.75 crore equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. The issue will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS), which means HCCH will not receive any money from the IPO. All proceeds will go to the selling shareholder.
The filing follows Coca-Cola's statement in June that it was exploring a potential listing of HCCH in 2027. HCCH is the parent entity of Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB), the company's Indian bottling arm.
HCCH's beverage portfolio and distribution network
HCCH operates across three beverage categories: sparkling, hydration and stills, including juices. Its activities include preparing, packaging, distributing and selling beverages, with its portfolio comprising 41 products as of June 30, 2026.
The company had a distribution network spanning around 1.7 million retail outlets, supported by 2,273 distributors, as of June 30, 2026.
The TKC Report cited in the DRHP identifies HCCH as the largest non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (NARTD) beverage company by revenue among businesses operating exclusively in India in FY26. It also ranks the company as the largest bottler within the Coca-Cola System in India, based on units of concentrate sold.
HCCH's retained units reported revenue from operations of Rs 4,310.17 crore for the three months ended June 30, 2026, registering a year-on-year increase of 20.46 per cent. Total sales volume grew 18.61 per cent over the same period.
Who owns HCCH?
The Coca-Cola Company held a 60 per cent stake in HCCH through Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd as of the DRHP filing date. The remaining 40 per cent was owned by Jubilant Beverages Ltd, which became one of HCCH's promoters in July 2025.
The proposed listing also comes amid Coca-Cola's global asset-light strategy, under which the beverage major has been divesting its bottling assets. India is its fifth-largest market globally.
In 2024, the company transferred its bottling operations in Rajasthan, Bihar, the Northeast and parts of West Bengal to existing bottlers through franchise arrangements. These transactions generated $290 million (around Rs 2,420 crore) for Coca-Cola.
Kandhari Global Beverages, SLMG Beverages and Moon Beverages were awarded the franchises.
HCCB's manufacturing footprint in India
Coca-Cola operates in India through two entities: Coca-Cola India and Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB). Incorporated in February 1997, HCCB operates 14 bottling plants across the country.
The company is headquartered in Bengaluru, with operations spread across 10 states. Its manufacturing and sales portfolio includes Coca-Cola, Thums Up, Sprite, Minute Maid, Maaza, SmartWater, Kinley, Limca and Fanta, among others.
Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Citigroup Global Markets India, JP Morgan India, Morgan Stanley India Company, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

briefs.headline: Elon Musk's dream vehicle to cease production - What went wrong with Tesla Cybertruck
briefs.deck: Tesla is set to cease Cybertruck production by mid-2027 as it pivots towards the Cybercab robotaxi initiative. The Cybertruck's sales have disappointed, falling short of Elon Musk's ambitious expectations. Its avant-garde design polarized opinions within the automotive sphere, while Musk's contentious political stances have further tarnished brand loyalty. Nonetheless, some enthusiasts mourn the…
briefs.bodyText:
Tesla's Cybertruck arrived with big ambitions, a futuristic design and 
Elon Musk
's backing.
Now, it is bidding adieu.
The high-tech pickup was meant to shake up the automobile industry, but its journey is coming to an end. Musk announced on Friday that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production around the middle of 2027 at its facility outside Austin, Texas.
The move will make room for increased production of the company's Cybercab robotaxi, as Tesla shifts its focus towards autonomous vehicles.
But what led to the Cybertruck's early exit? A combination of disappointing sales, a price tag that was much higher than initially promised and growing controversy surrounding Musk.
1. Sales and pricing failed to meet expectations
Musk had projected annual production of 250,000 Cybertrucks, but sales remained far below that target. Kelley Blue Book estimated that Tesla sold just 20,237 units last year, around half the previous year's sales. Sales through September this year fell another 28%. Spencer Penn, a former Tesla executive who left before the Cybertruck's launch and now heads software developer LightSource, said electric trucks had struggled to attract demand.
“A really controversial vehicle unveiled by a controversial individual into a market where none of the electric trucks have been able to really capture demand,” he said.
Pricing was another hurdle. Musk had promised a price tag below $40,000, but the first Cybertrucks sold for double that amount or more. Penn, who had booked a pre-sale reservation, eventually decided against buying one after the promised price failed to materialise.
2. Its design made it impossible to ignore
With its sharp angles and stainless-steel body, the Cybertruck looked more like a science-fiction vehicle than a conventional pickup. Its 2019 unveiling grabbed attention when a Tesla designer threw a metal ball at its supposedly unbreakable glass, only for the window to shatter. A second attempt on another window ended the same way. Musk, however, remained convinced about his vision.
“I just wanted to make a futuristic battle tank — something that looks like it could come out of ‘Blade Runner’ or ‘Aliens’ or something like that but was also highly functional,” he told Automotive News.
He called it “a better sports car than a Porsche 911” and “a better truck than an F-150.” The design drew both admiration and ridicule. Armen Hareyan, whose Torque News site covers autos, said: “Few vehicles in history have generated as much attention. The Cybertruck became a cultural symbol – loved, mocked and impossible to ignore.”
Penn initially found its appearance revolting and called it “madness”, but his opinion changed the more he looked at it. He eventually saw it as an example of Tesla's adventurous spirit and willingness to take risks. “Some of these bets work and some of these bets don’t,” he said.
3. Musk's political image became a problem for some customers
Musk's association with several right-wing figures, particularly US President Donald Trump, alienated some Tesla customers. As his image shifted from an eccentric innovator to a polarising figure trading his billions for political influence, some previously passionate owners rushed to sell their cars. Others put stickers on their bumpers reading, “I bought this before Elon went crazy.”
The backlash extended to demonstrations outside Tesla showrooms, with organisers also urging investors to sell their shares. Some protests turned violent, with Molotov cocktails thrown at Tesla vehicles, charging stations set ablaze and dealerships covered in graffiti. Cybertruck owners faced hostility too, with some being shouted at with “Nazi!” and receiving extended middle fingers.
Ross Blankenship, a Cybertruck owner, said that he disliked seeing a vehicle he loved turned into a political symbol. Its futuristic appearance had reminded him of “Halo”, the science-fiction video game he played as a child.
“I had that sort of child in me wanting to be part of something cool that would change the future of automotive,” Blankenship said in a call from his Cybertruck as he drove through Sunnyside, Colorado.
Although he said he agreed with Musk on politics, he was unhappy about the vehicle becoming associated with the controversy.
“I never bought it for any other reason than the fascination with the future technology of trucks … so that was a little heartbreaking.” The Cybertruck's discontinuation also comes as Tesla shifts its attention towards autonomous vehicles. Musk said winding down production would allow the company to make more Cybercab robotaxis, a segment on which he is betting Tesla's future.
For a vehicle that Musk once called Tesla's best product, the planned shutdown marks an unceremonious end to a much-hyped project. Yet, it has not lost all its fans. Blankenship said he would buy another Cybertruck again in a heartbeat. He called the end of its production “a sad moment.”

briefs.headline: Muhurat Trading 2026: Why Dalal Street opens for an hour on Diwali - 10 stocks to buy
briefs.deck: Muhurat Trading will occur on Sunday, November 8, signaling the beginning of Samvat 2083. This trading session reflects auspiciousness associated with the Diwali festival and investor optimism. Major indices have seen strong rallies leading up to this event, driven by foreign investments and stable domestic economic indicators. Analysts recommend focusing on quality stocks and maintaining…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Diwali season is a holiday for most, but Dalal Street refuses to let the festive mood go to waste!
For one special hour, the trading terminals light up and investors get a shot at starting the new year with a good ‘Muhurat.’
That is the charm of 
Muhurat Trading
, the annual Diwali session when the stock exchanges open their doors for a brief spell. More than just another trading session, it marks the beginning of Samvat, the traditional Hindu financial year, and is seen as an auspicious time to begin new investments.
The roots of the tradition lie in Diwali's association with wealth and prosperity. During the Lakshmi Puja, devotees worship Goddess Lakshmi, while businesses perform Chopda Puja, offering prayers before their account books, cash boxes and financial records, seeking prosperity in the year ahead.
Over time, this age-old practice found a place on Dalal Street. Investors began buying and selling shares during the special Diwali session as a symbolic way of welcoming the new Samvat.
The ritual may have moved from account books to trading screens, but its central idea remains the same: start the financial year on an auspicious note.
When is Muhurat Trading 2026? Mark your clocks
Muhurat Trading will take place on Sunday, November 8, on Diwali.
- Pre-opening session: 2:05 pm to 2:20 pm
- Main equity trading session: 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm
The special session comes on the back of a strong rally. The Sensex ended the week up over 8.8%, one of its best weekly gains in recent times, as foreign funds returned to Indian stocks. 
The US midterm polls raised hopes of policy stability and a diplomatic resolution to the West Asia war, which pulled crude prices down by about 20% in under two weeks.
The index’s seven-session pre-Diwali run of 10.6% was its best in 35 years, adding 7,782 points. On Friday alone, it gained 1,781 points, its third straight session of four-figure gains, despite an overnight crash in the US market led by a rout in AI stocks.
Foreign portfolio investors drove the surge, buying Indian stocks worth about Rs 49,500 crore (roughly $5.2 billion) on a net basis, per NSDL and BSE data.
10 stocks to watch in Samvat 2083
Here are 10 picks from SBICAP Securities, PL and Motilal Oswal, along with their reported prices and potential upside.
- Tata Steel: Brokerage SBICAP Securities has pegged the steel major at Rs 200, about 17% above its current price of Rs 171. Access to captive iron ore and a plan to lift India capacity to 40 million tonnes by FY31 support the company’s growth story.
- MCX: Trading at Rs 3,187, the exchange operator has a target of Rs 3,633, a potential gain of 14%. SBI points to its near-99% share of commodity derivatives and an EBITDA margin of roughly 72% in FY26. That is a lot of market to call your own.
- SPR Auto Components: SPR Auto Components is trading at Rs 4,374, and Motilal Oswal Wealth Management has set a target of Rs 6,150, indicating a potential upside of 41%. The brokerage expects the auto components maker to benefit from strong demand and its expansion plans. 
- Bharat Electronics: PL Capital sees the defence PSU climbing from Rs 395 to Rs 490, a 24.1% upside. A Rs 68,720 crore order book, along with openings in radar, missile and drone technologies, supports that view.
- ICICI Bank: Priced at Rs 1,500, the lender is seen heading to Rs 1,900, or 26.7% higher. PL Capital expects loan growth, stable margins and healthy interest and fee income to back earnings.
- Blue Star: Starting from Rs 1,572, the air-conditioning major could cool its way to Rs 1,783, a 13.4% gain, says PL Capital. Low penetration of room ACs, rising demand for cooling and data-centre projects are expected to fuel growth.
- Titan: Motilal Oswal Wealth Management sees the jewellery-to-watches giant rallying 35% from Rs 4,437 to Rs 6,000. Strong jewellery demand, a push into premium products and a wider retail network are expected to add the sparkle.
- Adani Ports: Shares at Rs 1,850 could sail to Rs 2,130, a 15% rise, in Motilal Oswal Wealth Management’s assessment. The brokerage projects cargo volumes to expand at a 14% compound annual rate between FY26 and FY28.
- Shaily Engineering: The plastics engineering firm, currently at Rs 3,170, has an upside of 29% to Rs 4,074 in the brokerage’s estimate. Opportunities in GLP-1 injection pens, healthcare platforms and electronics are seen powering growth.
- Arvind: Motilal Oswal Wealth Management has set a Rs 670 target for the textile company, 37% above its current Rs 491. Growth in garments and advanced materials is expected to stitch together higher revenue and profit.
What does the market outlook for Samvat 2083 look like? 
The new Samvat year arrives with a mixed bag for Dalal Street.
Domestic economic fundamentals are holding firm, but geopolitical tensions, pricey crude oil, foreign investors heading for the exit and a wobbly currency are making sure the road ahead isn’t a smooth one.
Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, in its annual Muhurat investment outlook, expects Indian equities to deliver moderate returns in Samvat 2083. Its advice: put asset allocation and quality stocks first, and stop chasing short-term momentum like it’s the last auto-rickshaw home.
The fund house pointed to India’s projected GDP growth of 7.1% in FY27, backed by domestic demand and a broad-based economic recovery. There’s some valuation comfort on offer too. Large and mid-cap stocks look relatively reasonable, with major indices trading at a discount to their long-term average valuations as of October 31, 2026.
For the year ahead, Kotak Mutual Fund says it will stick to quality companies, disciplined asset allocation and long-term investing, rather than sprinting after every passing rally.
Don’t mistake that for a victory lap, though. The mood is caution, not unbridled optimism. Geopolitical tensions, swings in crude oil prices and a hawkish stance from global central banks could keep markets bumpy.
The takeaway for Samvat 2083 is simple: be choosy, keep your eyes on company fundamentals, and don’t expect fireworks-level returns once the Diwali ones fizzle out.

stories.headline: ‘Not a long-term solution’: Ex-cricketer questions Gautam Gambhir’s strategy
stories.deck: Dodda Ganesh has raised eyebrows over India's choice to position Axar Patel at the fifth spot in the batting lineup. He expresses that this approach limits KL Rahul's potential to elevate his batting status. In the second ODI versus New Zealand, India's middle order faced challenges under pressure following early wicket losses.
stories.bodyText:
Former India cricketer Dodda Ganesh has questioned India's decision to use Axar Patel at No. 5 in overseas conditions, arguing that the all-rounder should not be considered a long-term option at that batting position. He also felt the team management's approach was coming at the expense of KL Rahul's opportunity to spend more time at the crease.
Reacting to India's batting order during the second ODI against New Zealand in Wellington, Ganesh took to X to express his reservations about Axar's suitability for the role, particularly in SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia).
"I say it again: Axar Patel can’t be your no 5 in SENA countries. He could play a cameo here and there but he’s definitely not a long term solution. You are denying KL Rahul the game time #NZvIND," Ganesh wrote.
Dodda Ganesh's post
The former cricketer's comments come amid India's continued experimentation with their middle-order combinations. The team has often pushed Rahul down to No. 6 to maintain a left-right batting combination, with Axar getting an opportunity higher up the order.
That strategy came under scrutiny during the rain-affected second ODI, where India's batting line-up struggled against New Zealand's disciplined pace attack while chasing a target of 135.
After the visitors' bowlers had bundled out New Zealand for 134, India found themselves in early trouble on a surface offering bounce and movement. Jacob Duffy struck twice, dismissing captain 
Shubman Gill
 for a first-ball duck and Virat Kohli for seven, while Rohit Sharma managed 23 off 28 deliveries before departing.
Axar, promoted to No. 5, could contribute only seven runs before falling while attempting a ramp shot. Shreyas Iyer made 30 off 46 balls but failed to convert his start, leaving India under pressure at 47/4.
Rahul, meanwhile, provided the stability India desperately needed. Initially cautious, he negotiated the challenging conditions before shifting gears with a couple of pull shots, including a six. He remained unbeaten on 26 as India reached 113/7 in 26 overs when rain brought the contest to an end.
India were four runs ahead of the DLS par score at that stage, securing a four-wicket victory and taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match series.
The bowling effort had laid the foundation for the win, with Gurnoor Brar claiming career-best figures of 4/30. Auqib Nabi picked up 2/31, while Anshul Kamboj returned 2/25. New Zealand were eventually dismissed for 134 in 41 overs, with Daryl Mitchell top-scoring with 55.
Ganesh's remarks have once again brought the spotlight on India's middle-order strategy and whether Rahul should be given a higher batting position instead of being pushed down to accommodate the left-right combination.

stories.headline: Rohit Sharma enters record books with historic feat in rain-hit Wellington ODI
stories.deck: During the second ODI, Rohit Sharma set a new record for the most sixes hit against New Zealand in One-Day Internationals, breaking Shahid Afridi’s previous record by launching two sixes off Kyle Jamieson. Although rain interrupted play, India managed to secure a narrow four-run victory using the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method. Sharma’s significant contribution helped anchor the innings, giving…
stories.bodyText:
Rohit Sharma
 etched his name in ODI history on Saturday as he became the batter with the most sixes against New Zealand in the 50-over format. The India opener achieved the milestone during the second ODI at Hnry Stadium in Wellington, moving past former Pakistan all-rounder Shahid Afridi's long-standing record.
Rohit needed two sixes to surpass Afridi's tally of 50 maximums against the Black Caps and reached the landmark during his 23-run knock off 28 deliveries in India's chase of 135. The 39-year-old brought up the record with two sixes off New Zealand pacer Kyle Jamieson, one each in the seventh and ninth overs.
The Mumbai batter, who had registered a six-ball duck in the series opener in Auckland on Wednesday, bounced back with a couple of maximums to take his tally to 51 sixes in 34 innings across 36 ODIs against New Zealand.
Afridi had struck 50 sixes in 35 innings from 38 matches against the Black Caps between 1996 and 2015. West Indies great Chris Gayle occupies the third spot with 45 sixes, while former Sri Lanka opener Sanath Jayasuriya is fourth with 41. England's Jos Buttler and India's Virat Kohli complete the top six with 29 sixes each.
Most ODI sixes against New Zealand
Rohit's milestone came in a rain-affected contest that saw India take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the five-match series. 
India were chasing a modest target of 135 in a match reduced to 47 overs per side but found themselves in a difficult position at 113/7 after 26 overs when rain brought the contest to a halt.
With India needing another 23 runs and only three wickets remaining, New Zealand appeared to have a chance of pulling off a comeback. However, India were four runs ahead of the required score under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method when play was abandoned, handing them a four-run victory.
New Zealand's bowlers had made life difficult for the visitors, with Jamieson and Jacob Duffy sharing six wickets between them. Both finished with identical figures of 3/35, with Duffy removing 
Shubman Gill
 for a first-ball duck and Kohli for seven.
India had slipped to 47/4 before Shreyas Iyer steadied the innings with 30 off 46 balls. Rohit's 23 also provided some stability, while KL Rahul remained unbeaten on 26 when the rain intervened.
India subsequently lost Naman Dhir and Anshul Kamboj in quick succession after reaching 86/5, leaving the lower order with a challenging task. However, the rain ended New Zealand's hopes of defending the total, with the match eventually called off amid a heavy shower at around 11 pm local time.
The result gave India their second successive DLS victory in the series after they had beaten New Zealand by five wickets in the opening ODI in Auckland, where the hosts were bowled out for 185.

stories.headline: India hockey coach Gurdial Singh Bhangu dies at 86
stories.deck: Bhangu’s name will forever be associated with one of the most memorable victories in Indian women’s hockey: India’s 3-2 victory over England in the final at Manchester, becoming Commonwealth Games champions
stories.bodyText:
Gurdial Singh Bhangu, the coach who masterminded India's historic women's hockey gold medal at the 2002 Commonwealth Games, has died in Surrey, Canada.
He was aged 86.
"Hockey India mourns the sad demise of the Chief Coach of the 2002 Commonwealth Games Gold Medal-winning Indian Women’s Team, Shri Gurdial Singh Bhangu, at the age of 86. His contribution to Indian hockey will always be remembered. Our heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones," the federation wrote alongwith a post in 'X'
Bhangu's name will forever be associated with one of the most memorable victories in Indian women's hockey. Under his guidance, India defeated England 3-2 in the final at Manchester, becoming Commonwealth Games champions in a campaign that left a lasting impression on the country's sporting landscape.
The dramatic contest was settled by Mamta Kharab, whose extra-time goal secured India's victory after captain Suraj Lata Devi and her teammates had battled their way through a demanding tournament. The triumph subsequently became part of popular sporting culture, inspiring the storyline of the Shah Rukh Khan-starrer Chak De! India, released in 2007.
While the fictional character Kabir Khan, played by Shah Rukh Khan, was inspired by former India goalkeeper Mir Ranjan Negi, Bhangu was the man who masterminded the team's historic success in Manchester.
His tactical awareness and understanding of the game played a significant role in the dramatic final against England. Knowing that an attacking penalty-corner sequence could continue even after the final hooter, Bhangu had instructed his players to remain alert until the play was completed.
That advice proved decisive in extra time. As the hooter sounded, England's defenders momentarily switched off, but the Indian players continued their attack. Kharab capitalised on a rebound to put the ball into the net and send India on course for a historic victory.
Although the goal was initially ruled out, the decision was subsequently overturned by the officials, confirming India's memorable triumph.
Born in Lyallpur, now Faisalabad in Pakistan, Bhangu grew up in Ambala and played hockey at the university level. He later underwent coaching training at the National Institute of Sports in Patiala, where he had the opportunity to learn from hockey great Dhyan Chand and Olympic gold medallist Balkishan Singh.
Bhangu had considerable international coaching experience before taking charge of the Indian women's team. Between 1972 and 1976, he served as chief coach of the Nigerian women's hockey team, helping the side qualify for its first Women's Hockey World Cup in 1976.
He took over as India's chief coach in 1998, following the team's 12th-place finish at the Women's Hockey World Cup. Under his guidance, India claimed the silver medal at the Bangkok Asian Games later that year, setting the stage for their Commonwealth Games breakthrough four years later.
His contribution to Indian hockey was recognised with the Dronacharya Award in 2000, making him the first hockey coach to receive the prestigious national coaching honour.
Bhangu's legacy will remain closely associated with India's historic 2002 Commonwealth Games triumph, a victory that elevated women's hockey in the country and inspired generations of players.

stories.headline: Towhid Hridoy hits record-breaking double century for Bangladesh in second Test against West Indies
stories.deck: Hridoy became the fourth Bangladeshi batter to hit a double century after Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan and Tamim Iqbal and also passed Mushfiqur’s 219 to become the highest individual scorer for the country
stories.bodyText:
Bangladesh batter Towhid Hridoy converted his maiden century into a double century to lift his team into a dominant position in the second and final cricket test against West Indies on Saturday.
His masterclass helped Bangladesh reach 386, taking a 30-run lead in the first innings from a near-hopeless situation. West Indies was 7 for no loss when bad light forced early stump.
Hridoy was unbeaten on 242 off 359, smashing 22 fours and 11 sixes.
He became the fourth Bangladeshi batter to hit a double century after Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan and Tamim Iqbal and also passed Mushfiqur's 219 to become the highest individual scorer for the country.
The batter led the side astutely when Bangladesh appeared to concede a big first innings lead after West Indies was bowled out for 356.
“It's unbelievable how he was still able to find boundaries and hit sixes even when he started getting tired,” Bangladesh coach Phil Simmons said of Hridoy. “He showed outstanding game awareness, knowing which shots to play and when to give the last three batsmen the strike. Everything he did in this innings was exceptional.”
Resuming at 88-3 on Day 3, Hridoy and Mushfiqur negotiated the West Indies bowlers well before Jomel Warrican dismissed Mushfiqur, ending their 73-run partnership.
Warrican and skipper Roston Chase then sparked a collapse as Bangladesh lost three wickets in quick succession to be left at 184-7.
Hridoy then helped the side stage a comeback by adding 117 runs with Taijul Islam in the eighth wicket.
He raised his maiden century off 171 balls, taking a single off Chase, which also took the side past 300.
After the century, Hridoy became more adventurous, unleashing a spectacular attack on West Indies bowlers. Ten of his 11 sixes, highest by any Bangladeshi batter and also second highest in cricket history, came in in this period, leaving visiting bowlers shocked.
Warrican, who took 4-104, finally broke through with the wicket of Taijul for 22.
But Hridoy was unstoppable, as he shared an 85-run partnership with Taskin Ahmed in the ninth wicket to edge Bangladesh ahead.
He raised his double century of 304 balls by driving Warrican to long-off for single.
“We were thinking about what lead we could have got or how big the lead could have been, but the way Hridoy batted was special,” Warrican said. “We have to reflect on things that we could have done better. As a unit, we still have to keep our heads up because there's a job to be done. We have to come back well tomorrow.”
Jayden Seales dismissed Taskin to wrap up Bangladesh innings as opener Shadman Islam was unable to bat after injuring his ankle on Day 2.
Bangladesh bowlers lost two reviews in the first over before West Indies openers Joshua da Silva and Brandon King kept them unscathed by safely negotiating four overs.

Hardik Pandya’s absence from competitive cricket will continue, with the all-rounder missing from Baroda’s 15-member squad for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, India’s domestic T20 tournament.
His brother Krunal Pandya has been named captain of the side. Hardik last featured in competitive cricket on May 24 during an IPL 2026 fixture for Mumbai Indians.
The all-rounder was initially included in India A’s one-day squad for the October series against Australia A but had to withdraw after suffering a fresh shin injury. According to ESPNcricinfo, Hardik was not completely pain-free while bowling at the time.
Since the conclusion of the IPL, Hardik has spent considerable time at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, where he has been recovering from a series of fitness setbacks, including back spasms sustained during the IPL and a subsequent leg strain.
His last international appearance came in the T20I series against New Zealand at home, shortly before the start of IPL 2026.
India, currently engaged in the ODI series against New Zealand, are scheduled to return to T20I action in December for a home series against Sri Lanka.
With the ODI World Cup in Africa scheduled for next year, India would be keen to have their premier T20 all-rounder back in the mix as early as possible. Hardik’s return to action will be crucial as the team looks to build combinations and fine-tune its preparations ahead of the marquee tournament.
The Baroda squad, led by Krunal Pandya, also features several prominent names, including Jitesh Sharma, Deepak Hooda and Rasikh Salam. They will begin their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy campaign against Chandigarh in Mumbai on November 14.

briefs.headline: Jaiswal smashes second ton of the A tour, hits top form ahead of Test series
briefs.deck: Jaiswal (102 off 138), whose form became a matter of concern after the first red ball game of the tour, has regained his sublime touch ahead of the two Test series beginning on November 19
briefs.bodyText:
Yashasvi Jaiswal scored an intent filled hundred, his second consecutive first-class hundred, steering India A to 227 for two at stumps on day one of the third unofficial Test against New Zealand A in Lincoln, New Zealand, on Saturday.
Jaiswal (102 off 138), whose form became a matter of concern after the first red ball game of the tour, has regained his sublime touch ahead of the two Test series beginning on November 19.
Play was called off after rain lashed the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in the 70th over of the day. The pitch had a greenish look to it but the Indian batters had a good time batting on it.
Sai Sudharsan (77 batting off 205) and captain Dhruv Jurel (12 batting off 24) were in the middle when the stumps were drawn.
The game has added significance with the presence of Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja and Prasidh Krishna who are the playing the final India A game as part of their preparation for the Test series.
The day well and truly belonged to Jaiswal, who batted aggressively against the New Zealand A pacers, smashing them all around the park. On display were a host of cut shots, pulls and delightful cover drives.
The left-hander got to his half century with a copybook cover drive off seamer Brett Randell. He was particularly harsh on Jarrod Mckay, picking him for three straight boundaries twice in his innings. His dropped catch on 54 added to the woes of home team.
Jaiswal also hit couple of sixes in his entertaining knock and one of them was a massive hit over mid-on off Zak Gibson.
He got into the 90s with a rasping cut shot off Cameron Paul before completing his century with a sweep shot in the 44th over bowled by off-spinner Dean Foxcroft. He departed soon after as he guided a full ball straight into the hands of the mid-off fielder off Ferns.
Mckay removed the in-form Devdutt Padikkal in the 63rd over. Padikkal went for an expansive drive only to be caught behind.
Sudharsan was going strong before rain halted proceedings. His innings too had a bunch of perfectly placed pull shots and crisp cover drives.
The first two games ended in draws.

briefs.headline: Shami defined an era of pace bowling: BCCI
briefs.deck: “Thank you for defining an era of Indian pace bowling, Test Cap #279,” wrote the BCCI said
briefs.bodyText:
The BCCI on Saturday paid a glowing tribute Mohammad Shami, saying the wily India pacer defined an era of pace bowling in Test cricket.
Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday night. He ended his Test journey with 229 wickets from 64 matches, making him the sixth most successful pacer in Tests for the country behind Kapil Dev (434), Zaheer Khan, Ishant Sharma (both 311), Javagal Srinath (236), Jasprit Bumrah (234).
"Thank you for defining an era of Indian pace bowling, Test Cap #279," wrote the BCCI on social media.
Former India cricketers also joined in to congratulate Shami on a successful red ball career. Ravi Shastri believes Shami had more red ball cricket left in him.
"Incredible career. I was lucky that I was the coach at that time. He was instrumental in India doing well. Without him the fast bowling unit would not have functioned. No one presented the seam better than him in world cricket. You could say James Anderson as well. If Shami did not get the wickets, he would still keep the pressure on the opposition.
"Sad to see him go. I definitely though he had another 30-40 wickets left in him. He should have played in the last 12 months. May be should have been on this New Zealand tour as a Test match bowler," Shastri told the host broadcaster during the second ODI in New Zealand.
"Many congratulations on your wonderful red ball cricket career @MdShami11. Your late movement with that cherry will be missed," wrote Pathan.
"You will be Missed in Whites Buddy, congratulations on your amazing career. See you soon in Blues," added another former India pacer Munaf Patel.
His Bengal teammate Manoj Tiwary said it was an honour playing alongside Shami.
"The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history.
"This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart," said Tiwary.

briefs.headline: Adkar, Bhosale become first Indian women's pair to reach final at main WTA Tour level
briefs.deck: India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale made history at the Chennai Open, becoming the first all-Indian women’s pair to reach a main WTA Tour doubles final. They defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, 10-8 after a thrilling comeback in the super tie-break. They will face Swiss duo Naima Karamoko and Simona Waltert in the final.
briefs.bodyText:
India's Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale scripted history at the Chennai Open on Saturday, becoming the first all-Indian women's pair to reach a doubles final at the main WTA Tour level. The duo defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska of Poland and Alana Smith of the USA 6-2, 2-6, 10-8 in a hard-fought semifinal.
The Indian pair started strongly but lost their rhythm in the second set.
However, they showed great determination in the deciding super tie-break to seal the memorable victory in front of the home crowd.
A historic achievement for Indian tennis
No all-Indian women's combination had previously reached a final at the main WTA Tour level. While Shikha Uberoi and her sister Neha reached finals in 2005, Neha represented the USA at the time.
Former Indian star Sania Mirza also enjoyed tremendous success in doubles, winning 43 titles, but never achieved those victories with an Indian partner.
Ankita Raina and Karman Thandi won a WTA 125 doubles title in 2018, but that tournament belongs to a level below the main Tour.
Adkar and Bhosale will now face Swiss pair Naima Karamoko and Simona Waltert in the final. 
The Swiss duo booked their place after defeating Isabelle Haverlag and Panna Udvardy 6-4, 6-4.
How the Indians pulled off the victory
Adkar and Bhosale dominated the opening set, taking a 4-1 lead by making the most of their opponents' mistakes before winning it 6-2.
However, Falkowska and Smith bounced back in the second set, taking advantage of missed break opportunities and errors from the Indian pair to win it 6-2 and force a decider.
The super tie-break was equally tense, with the opponents opening up a 3-0 lead. The Indians fought back despite trailing 6-8, with Bhosale producing a crucial forehand winner before Adkar delivered a winning volley to earn match point. She then sealed the contest with a brilliant forehand down the line, completing the historic 10-8 victory.
Meanwhile, top seed and defending champion Janice Tjen defeated Robin Montgomery 6-3, 6-4 to enter the women's singles final. Third seed Magda Linette also advanced after beating Anastasia Zakharova 2-6, 6-2, 6-3.

briefs.headline: How much more can Carlos Alcaraz earn after securing €290,960 at Paris Masters 2026?
briefs.deck: Carlos Alcaraz has reached his first Paris Masters semi-final after saving two match points to defeat Taylor Fritz in a dramatic comeback. The Spaniard now faces Casper Ruud for a place in Sunday's final, with €974,370 in prize money awaiting the champion. A victory would guarantee Alcaraz €532,120 and boost his ranking points ahead of the season's conclusion.
briefs.bodyText:
Carlos Alcaraz has reached the semi-finals of the Paris Masters for the first time, but his route to the last four was far from straightforward. The Spaniard saved two match points against Taylor Fritz before completing a three-set comeback, keeping alive his hopes of reaching a maiden final in Paris. A meeting with Casper Ruud now stands between him and a place in Sunday's championship match, with almost €1 million awaiting the eventual winner.
Alcaraz has €974,370 in his sights at the Paris Masters
Carlos Alcaraz, who is making his sixth appearance at the Paris Masters, has historically found the tournament a challenging venue. The fast indoor hard courts have made it one of his toughest events on the Masters 1000 circuit, and before this year, he had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals. Having finally reached his maiden semi-final, the Spaniard has already secured €290,960. He will face Casper Ruud on Saturday, November 7, with a victory guaranteeing him €532,120 as the runner-up and putting the tournament's €974,370 winner's cheque within reach.
Tennis - ATP 1000 Masters - Paris Masters - Plenitude Arena, Nanterre, France - November 6, 2026 Spain's Carlos Alcaraz celebrates after winning his quarter final match against Taylor Fritz of the U.S
According to the ATP Tour's official prize-money breakdown, the 2026 men's singles champion will collect €974,370, while the runner-up receives €532,120. 
The two players who lose their semi-final matches are each awarded €290,960.
The financial difference between the remaining stages is considerable. Beating Ruud would increase Alcaraz's guaranteed earnings by €241,160, while winning the final would take his tournament payout €683,410 above the amount awarded for a semi-final exit. The difference between finishing first and second is €442,250.
- Champion: €974,370
- Runner-up: €532,120
- Semi-finalist: €290,960
These awards are determined by a player's final position and are not cumulative. Alcaraz will receive the amount corresponding to his eventual finish rather than adding the payments for each round. The figures also represent tournament prize money before any applicable taxes or expenses.
The ATP lists the total prize pool for the event at €6,309,095, covering the tournament as a whole rather than the men's singles competition alone.
Alcaraz saves two match points to overturn Taylor Fritz
The Spaniard's first Paris Masters semi-final came after one of the most demanding matches of his campaign. Alcaraz defeated Taylor Fritz 6-7(10), 7-5, 6-3 in a quarter-final lasting two hours and 45 minutes, recovering from a position in which the American was twice within a point of victory.
Fritz took the opening set in a lengthy tie-break, leaving Alcaraz needing to win the next two sets to stay in the tournament. The American then moved into a 5-3 lead in the second set, putting himself in a strong position to close out the match.
Alcaraz first saved a match point on his own serve before holding to reduce the deficit to 5-4. Fritz subsequently had another opportunity to finish the contest while serving for the match, but the Spaniard produced a blistering forehand passing shot to save the second match point and break back.
The momentum shifted decisively. Alcaraz won four consecutive games from 3-5 to take the second set 7-5, forcing a deciding set after appearing close to elimination.
He carried that momentum into the third, reducing his baseline errors and securing an early break before closing out the set 6-3. The victory also extended his head-to-head advantage over Fritz to 7-1.
The match had its share of moments that brought the Paris crowd into the contest. After producing a spectacular point to hold for 4-5 in the second set, Alcaraz encouraged the spectators as he attempted to turn the match around. His recovery from two match points ultimately secured a place in the tournament's final four for the first time.
When is Carlos Alcaraz vs Casper Ruud?
Alcaraz faces Casper Ruud in Saturday's semi-final, November 7, with the match scheduled to begin not before 9:30 PM IST. The Norwegian reached the last four after defeating Portugal's Nuno Borges 7-6(5), 6-4, continuing a run in which he had progressed through his first four matches in Paris without dropping a set.
Casper Ruud. (AP Photo)
The upcoming meeting gives Alcaraz an opportunity to reach a first Paris Masters final. He leads Ruud 6-1 in their ATP head-to-head record, although the Norwegian's form during the tournament makes him a significant obstacle.
The winner will advance to Sunday's final, scheduled for November 8, not before 7:30 PM IST, against Ben Shelton. Shelton has already secured his place in the championship match and will await the outcome of the Alcaraz-Ruud semi-final.
Ranking points provide another incentive
The prize money is not the only reward at stake for Alcaraz. The Paris Masters also offers a substantial opportunity to collect ranking points before the end of the season, with the ATP awarding 400 points to each losing semi-finalist, 650 to the runner-up and 1,000 to the champion.
Alcaraz has already guaranteed himself 400 points by reaching the last four. A victory over Ruud would raise that total to 650, while winning Sunday's final would give him the full 1,000 points available to the champion.
For the Spaniard, the immediate objective is to convert his first semi-final appearance in Paris into a maiden final. Having come within a point of leaving the tournament against Fritz, he now has an opportunity to finish the week competing for both its biggest prize and its most valuable ranking reward.

briefs.headline: ISL: Chennaiyin notches up first win in style
briefs.deck: Brison and Irfan score braces for the home team
briefs.bodyText:
It was a transformed Chennaiyin FC that turned up at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium here on Saturday.
Playing a brand of football it rarely displayed in its previous four matches, the host served up a pre-Deepavali treat to its fans with an impressive 5-3 win — its first of the season — over East Bengal FC in the Indian Super League.
Braces from Brison Fernandes and Irfan Yadwad, along with a penalty converted by Ramon Tanque, completed a dominant performance by the host.
Chennaiyin launched attacks from both flanks and through the centre, creating several chances.
Brison drew first blood after a fine pass from the right by Irfan. Unmarked, he fired a powerful right-footed shot past goalkeeper Prabhsukhan Gill. He then made it 2-0 with a strong strike from outside the box.
East Bengal struggled to break through Chennaiyin’s defence but reduced the margin through Ake Loba, who scored from close range after Daniel Ramirez dispossessed Ayush Dev and set him up.
Brison was in the thick of things again when Jeakson Singh brought him down inside the box. Ramon converted the resulting penalty.
A handball by Chennaiyin’s Muhammed Saheef early in the second half gifted East Bengal a penalty and Ramirez made no mistake. The visitor then showed greater purpose, attacking down the flanks.
However, Chennaiyin reasserted its supremacy when substitute Lalhriatpuia’s fierce shot was deflected into the net by Irfan. Soon the latter added his second with a fine finish after a through pass from Ramon.
The results: Chennaiyin FC 5 (Brison Fernandes 4, 18, Ramon Tanque 41-pen, Irfan Yadwad 59, 67) bt East Bengal FC 3 (Ake Loba 29, Daniel Ramirez 47-pen, David Hmar 90+1).
